Components / Reasoning

Confirmation

Human-in-the-loop approve/deny sized for a thumb. Renders NOTHING without an approval or while arguments are still streaming — the web contract, made total in a Vitest-owned phase machine. Once answered the pair stays: the chosen side resolves with a check, the other disables, and the outcome persists in the transcript (question.tsx's persistence, replacing the web's swap-to-Accepted/Rejected rows).

  • v0.2.1
  • component
  • nativewind
  • uniwind
  • runs in Expo Go

Install

npx @react-native-reusables/cli@latest add https://rnraielements.com/r/nativewind/confirmation.json
npx @react-native-reusables/cli@latest add https://rnraielements.com/r/uniwind/confirmation.json

Source

Props

NameTypeDefaultDescription
stateToolStatus—The tool part's state, streamed straight in.
approvalConfirmationApproval | null | undefined—The tool part's approval object. Omit it and the card renders nothing.
onRespond((approved: boolean) => void) | undefined—Fires once per decision. Wiring the outcome back is the caller's job.
childrenReact.ReactNode——

Theming

Themed via text-foreground.

Usage

() => ( <Confirmation state="input-available" approval={{ approved: true }} onRespond={() => {}}> <ConfirmationRequest> <ConfirmationTitle>Install 56 items into apps/example?</ConfirmationTitle> <ConfirmationActions> <ConfirmationAction action="approve">Install</ConfirmationAction> <ConfirmationAction action="deny">Skip</ConfirmationAction> </ConfirmationActions> </ConfirmationRequest> </Confirmation> )
